questions.title: Ball in a Footprint in the Bunker
questions.question: Your ball stops in a footprint made by someone else in the sand bunker. What can you do by the rules?

choices.text: Pick up your ball and drop it for free outside the footprint
Play the ball from the footprint or choose to say it’s unplayable
Move your ball to a better place in the bunker without any penalty
Ask your friend what to do and drop your ball again for free

questions.explanation: If your ball is in a footprint in the bunker, you have two choices: play it where it is, or call it unplayable, which means you add a penalty and follow the unplayable ball rule.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A bunker is a sandy area on the golf course, like a big sandpit.
Unplayable means you think it's too hard to hit the ball from where it is, and you take a penalty to move it.

questions.teachingTip: Let children practise playing balls out of footprints in a bunker, and also discuss what declaring 'unplayable' means and how to do it.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think they can always move the ball to a better place in the bunker if it lands in a footprint.
Some might believe they get a free drop when the ball is in a footprint.

questions.title: Playing a Ball from a Bad Lie
questions.question: Your ball comes to rest in an old footprint in a bunker. What are your options under the Rules of Golf?

choices.text: Take a free drop out of the footprint
Play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable
Move the ball to a better spot in the bunker without penalty
Ask your opponent for advice and re-drop without penalty

questions.explanation: When your ball is in a difficult lie such as an old footprint, you must either play it as it lies or declare it unplayable, which comes with a penalty.
